title: fix(app-shell): form designer field cards announce a localized role, not dnd-kit's English "sortable" (objectui#11872)
body:
Fixes #11872

Clause-②: no. An attribute value inside the designer and one engine string: no export, prop, `@object-ui/types` member or accepted input changes.

## What changes

- `SortableField` in `packages/app-shell/src/views/studio-design/ObjectFormDesigner.tsx` now passes `attributes.roleDescription` to its `useSortable` call. A writable card gets the engine string `engine.studio.designer.fieldRole`. A read-only package's card gets a blank value.
- `engine.studio.designer.fieldRole` sits beside `engine.studio.designer.fieldAria` in the designer's two engine tables, `ENGINE_STRINGS_EN` ("draggable field") and `ENGINE_STRINGS_ZH`. These are the only two tables the file keeps for these keys. The card reads it through the same `t(…, locale)` and `useMetadataLocale()` its `aria-label` already uses.
- New pin: `ObjectFormDesigner.roleDescription-11872.test.tsx`. Changeset: `.changeset/11872-form-roledescription.md` (`@object-ui/app-shell` patch).

Nothing else in either file changes. `formDndAnnouncements.ts`, the `DndContext` props, `formCollision`, the keyboard sensor, `packages/i18n/**` and `packages/components/src/ui/**` are untouched.

## Mechanism hypotheses, measured

- **H1: confirmed.** At the installed `@dnd-kit/sortable` 10.0.0 and `@dnd-kit/core` 6.3.1, `useSortable` hands `useDraggable` the object `{ ...defaultAttributes, ...userDefinedAttributes }`, where `defaultAttributes` is `{ roleDescription: 'sortable' }`. `useDraggable` writes it as `aria-roledescription`. Its own default, `'draggable'`, applies only when the value is `undefined`. Measured by the reverse check below: without the argument every card reads `sortable`, and with it every card reads the localized row.
- **H2: confirmed.** `{...attributes}` is spread before `aria-label`. The hook returns `role`, `tabIndex`, `aria-disabled`, `aria-pressed`, `aria-roledescription` and `aria-describedby`, and nothing after the spread writes `aria-roledescription`. In real Chromium the DOM attribute is exactly the row: "draggable field" in en, and the zh row in zh.
- **H3: the measured answer is no role description.** The read-only card still renders through `useSortable`. It is `role="button"` with `tabindex="0"`, a click opens the inspector, and it cannot be dragged, because the `DndContext` gets no sensors when `readOnly`. Inside the fenced call, a blank value is the only way to give it none: `undefined` falls through to `useDraggable`'s English `draggable`. Real Chromium exposes no `roledescription` property for a blank value, the same as for an absent attribute. The reading uses CDP `Accessibility.getFullAXTree` on a dev-only harness that mounts the real `ObjectFormDesigner` (not committed). Static control rows on the same page read: absent gives none, blank gives none, `sortable` gives `sortable`. So the read-only card reads as a plain button. This is pinned.
- **The group cards:** they are not sortable. `Section` calls only `useDroppable`, which returns no attributes. In both the test DOM and Chromium, the field cards are the only elements with `aria-roledescription`. There is no scope question.
- **Wording:** the suggested wording stays. Chromium exposes the en row verbatim. For zh, the DOM attribute is exactly the zh string. The DevTools AX readout of the `roledescription` property returns any non-ASCII text as its UTF-8 bytes read as Latin-1, and it does so for static HTML controls too (a zh one and a French one). That is the instrument's serialization, not this change. What a real screen reader speaks for the zh row is NOT MEASURED: this container has no screen reader.

## Reverse check

The fix was committed first (`dd86396`). `ablation-replace.mjs` then deleted the `attributes:` line: the anchor count went from 1 to 0 and the blob changed. The pin then failed 3 tests and passed 1. Each failing case (en, zh, read-only) received `aria-roledescription="sortable"`. As predicted, the group-sections case stayed green, because the three cards are still the only elements that carry the attribute. The restore was proven: the blob equals `HEAD` and `git diff HEAD` is empty. The pin went red, as predicted.

## Gates, on `abf200c` (after merging `origin/main` at `09821b1`)

- `pnpm --workspace-concurrency=2 --filter '@object-ui/app-shell^...' build`: exit 0 (29 of 47 projects).
- `pnpm --filter @object-ui/app-shell type-check`: exit 0. `tsconfig.test.json` lists the new test (one `--listFilesOnly` hit).
- `pnpm exec vitest run` over 8 files: the new pin, `ObjectFormDesigner.test.tsx`, `ObjectFormDesigner.dndAnnouncements-11802.test.tsx`, `ObjectFormDesigner.keyboardDrop-11871.test.tsx`, `StudioDesignSurface.readOnlyWording-11781.test.tsx`, `StudioDesignSurface.accessGuard.test.tsx`, `StudioDesignSurface.pillarNavGuard.test.tsx` and `metadata-admin/studio-locale.i18n.test.tsx`. Result: 8 files and 57 tests passed. No file in `metadata-admin` matches `i18n*.test.*`, and the literal `*.guard.test.*` glob matches no file in either directory, so the two `*Guard.test.tsx` files ran in its place.
- These all exit 0: `check:control-bytes`, `check:new-line-citations`, `check:changeset-claims`, `check:pending-changeset-literals`, `check:i18n-designer-parity`, `check:i18n-dead-keys`, `check:i18n-keys`, `check:i18n-drift`, `check:test-path-roots` and `check:vi-mock-specifiers`. Also `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs` and `pnpm changeset:check` exit 0, and `check-governed-queue-guard.mjs --test` over the four paths answers NOT GOVERNED.
- Not run locally: the repo-wide `pnpm lint` and the full test farm, which belong to CI. ESLint over the three touched source files exits 0, with one warning that was already there (`react-hooks/set-state-in-effect` on the draft re-sync effect, not on a changed line). That is a spot check, not a narrowing claim.

## Acceptance notes (seen, not changed here)

1. **A read-only card still carries the drag instructions as its accessible description.** On the same Chromium harness, a read-only package's field card computes the description "To pick up a field, press Space or Enter. While dragging, use the arrow keys to move it. …" in en, and the zh equivalent in zh. `useDraggable` always points `aria-describedby` at the `DndContext`'s instructions, and the `attributes` argument cannot remove that. A change needs either the card's JSX after the spread or the `DndContext` accessibility props (objectui#11802's surface). Both are outside this card's fence, so this goes to the seat.
2. **The same family elsewhere, read in source only.** Other `useSortable` call sites take dnd-kit's English default or hard-code English: `NavigationRenderer` in `packages/layout` (its `groupedReorder-11626` test pins `sortable`), `DashboardRenderer`, the `KanbanImpl` cards, `ManageViewsDialog`, and `ViewTabBar` (`roleDescription: 'view tab'`). This goes to the seat.
